title: FABRIK3D in Ready() not working
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in Godot version 4.6

### System information

Windows 10 - Godot v4.6 - Vulkan (Forward+)

### Issue description


Hi,

I am attempting to generate bones, solvers and targets ... within Ready() ... in flat code and without any associated functions ... and then use those solvers to bake animation cycles to the library.

Here is a CCDIK3D example,

[node_3d.gd](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1dAbu1WGOguNlV8do-ouKwAuNmcfMRNPC/view?usp=sharing)

Summery,
We successfully reproduced **CCDIK3D** in flat code by injecting values directly into the `settings/0/`paths and using `skeleton.advance(0)`. However, we are unable to get **FABRIK3D** to solve in the same way. Even when mirroring the chain structure and using the lifecycle flush, FABRIK returns Identity rotations. Is there a specific **internal resource initialization** required for FABRIK chains that differs from CCDIK settings when working script-only?

[CCDIK3D in Ready() not working](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/115643)

Upon further testing of **FABRIK**, We discovered that while CCDIK3D exposes its `settings/0/` properties to `get_property_list()` immediately in _ready(), FABRIK3D remains entirely empty. Even after setting `chain_count = 1`, FABRIK3D does not generate any property paths for its chains or joints. This makes it impossible to configure FABRIK via flat-code/script-only for baking purposes. Is FABRIK intended to be 'editor-only' for configuration, or is there a specific way to manually initialize its internal chain resources in script?
